clinician.final_diagnosis: Cervical myelopathy from spinal cord compression by arachnoid web
clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 60s with a history of atrial fibrillation status post-ablation and TURP presented with a 2-year history of gradually worsening gait imbalance, frequent falls, severe thoracic and lumbar back pain, and progressive lower limb weakness (left leg initially, then right leg involvement) without sensory symptoms. Within 3 months of symptom onset, his gait deteriorated from cane to walker dependence. Neurological examination revealed hyperreflexia in all four extremities, bilateral positive Babinski reflexes in the lower limbs, and a positive left-sided Hoffman reflex, consistent with upper motor neuron signs of myelopathy, despite normal strength graded at 5/5 bilaterally. After approximately 1.5 years of inconclusive prior diagnostic workup, repeat spinal imaging including CT myelogram and non-contrasted MRI of the thoracic spine identified an arachnoid web/cyst at thoracic vertebral levels T7-T8, characterized by minimal dorsal indentation along the spinal cord with a positive scalpel sign and no associated syrinx. The patient was subsequently referred for neurosurgical evaluation based on these imaging findings.
